description: Executable Candidate recipe for christopherowen's spark-ds41f release spark-ds41f-1107 (8e5ea208, 2026-11-07, Apache-2.0) serving DeepSeek's official DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (revision 1bae0e10, MIT) with vLLM on three Sparks with tensor parallelism 3. It cannot run the creator's measured shape and runs his own smaller one instead. The creator's TP3 profiles need a 64 KiB-page kernel with Memory Saver (1,048,576-token window, 5.27 GB KV pool, the embedding and head in a display carve-out) and, for the triangle, a switchless cabling; a recipe can choose neither a kernel nor a device bind. This recipe is his own stock 4 KiB-page profile tp3-triangle-4k, which he marks unqualified: 262,144-token window, up to 8 sequences, 4,096 batched tokens, a 2,362,232,012-byte KV pool, 512-token prefix-cache retention interval, the carve-out off (SPARK_DS41F_DISPLAY_CARVEOUT_WEIGHTS=0, his tp4-ring value; its effect at TP3 is unknown), on a switched fabric (his tp3-switched transport settings, a combination he has no profile for). The platform sets the NCCL interface and GID names, so the creator's are dropped; sparknet does not read NCCL_IB_HCA and discovers up to two active devices with an IPv4 RoCE v2 GID itself. The switched transport also sets the creator's traffic class 106 (NCCL_IB_TC and SPARKNET_ROCE_TRAFFIC_CLASS). It needs three Sparks on a switch; this fleet has two, so the recipe is installable but untested here. Everything else is the release's launch: DSpark with 5 greedy draft tokens, block rejection and adaptive verification at row cost 0.035, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, TileLang attention, linear and MoE backends, a disk Engram table, direct checkpoint loading, yielding a long prompt's chunk to short requests, the deepseek_v41 parsers, images (up to 67 per prompt) and his default sampling (temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0). His GLP-steered second served name needs a gated repository and is omitted. Engine: no image is published (spark-ds41f:1107 is a local tag), so the image is built from source: the fetch stage clones the release and runs spark-ds41f's own preparation against its lock (vLLM 19f2c20e with 641 patches, B12X 236ddff, NCCL 2.30.7 patched for sm_121, TileLang 2123e412, TileKernels, sparknet 0.5.0 with its one-shot RoCE collectives, CUTLASS 4.7.1) on the digest-pinned vllm/vllm-openai base, then the release's Dockerfile stages converted to the static build policy, with a build-time sm_121 kernel scan of the compiled extensions and NCCL. Interface fix: the direct loader, the Engram row reader and B12X need io_uring, which the sandbox blocks (the creator runs seccomp=unconfined). The image compiles them unchanged against a header-only liburing stand-in that does one pread() per read under the default seccomp profile, and the build check that they link liburing now asserts they link none. Loading and Engram reads may be slower than the creator's. Memory is an estimate: the non-Engram weights are about 307 GB, 102 GB per Spark, plus the 2.36 GB pool and the engine's overhead; the declared 118 GB peak is the creator's 1M-token measurement (at least 6.03 GiB of head MemAvailable) less the larger pool, rounded up, and does not count the embedding and head returning to regular memory with the carve-out off. Creator speeds are for his 1M shape and are not claimed. Licences are information only: weights MIT, spark-ds41f and sparknet Apache-2.0.
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 spark-ds41f 1107 vLLM three Sparks
